result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers make the same core fixes: real buttons with item-specific names, focus moving to the new view's heading along with a title change, prices in the alt text, bottom padding for the bar, and the original look kept. The deciding difference is order submission. B's placeholder shows 'Your order has been received' even though nothing is sent, so a live launch could tell members their order went through when it didn't. A's placeholder fails safely, shows an error that keeps what she typed, and says clearly that this must be wired up before launch. B does add a proper HTML head and asks the user to check the alt-text prices against the images, but that doesn't outweigh the false confirmation. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers turn the plus and minus divs into named buttons, move focus to the new view's heading, update the page title, put the prices in alt text and pad the page above the fixed bar, so they are close on the core fixes. A changes the look slightly less, but it shows a 'Thank you, your order has been received' view even though no order is sent, which could go live by mistake at the weekend launch. B's placeholder fails openly, keeps what the member typed and says plainly that orders are not sent yet, which is the safer choice; its added 'Total:' label and site-wide focus ring are small, defensible changes to the look.
